explanation: Mango: family Anacardiaceae, order Sapindales, class Dicotyledonae, division Angiospermae.
trap: Trap (A): Recalling the order of wheat for mango | Trap (B): Recalling the order that includes Solanaceae and Convolvulaceae | Trap (C): Giving the family of mango when the order is asked

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Diatom cell walls are embedded with silica and are indestructible. II. Gonyaulax is a dinoflagellate that causes red tides. III. Euglenoids have a rigid cellulosic cell wall. IV. Slime moulds are photosynthetic protists.
explanation: I and II are correct. Euglenoids have a pellicle instead of a cell wall; slime moulds are saprophytic protists.
trap: Trap (A): Rejecting statement II by associating red tides with red algae | Trap (C): Also accepting statement III, ignoring that euglenoids have a flexible protein-rich pellicle | Trap (D): Also accepting statement IV, although slime moulds are saprophytic

question: A vascular bundle in which xylem and phloem lie on the same radius with cambium between them is
explanation: Same radius = conjoint; cambium present = open. This is typical of dicot stems; monocot bundles are conjoint and closed.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing same radius with the alternate arrangement in roots and ignoring cambium | Trap (B): Remembering conjoint correctly but treating presence of cambium as closed | Trap (C): Getting open right but calling the same-radius arrangement radial

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Marginal (b) Parietal (c) Free central (d) Basal. Column II: (i) Primrose (ii) Marigold (iii) Pea (iv) Argemone.
explanation: Marginal – pea; parietal – mustard, Argemone; free central – Dianthus, primrose; basal – sunflower, marigold.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping marginal and parietal, since both have ovules on the ovary wall | Trap (C): Swapping parietal and free central examples | Trap (D): Swapping primrose and marigold between free central and basal
review_note: Faculty flag: Match item shares its option codes and key (B) with P1-050 and P2-110 (template similarity 0.85; different facts).

question: In a pea flower the largest petal overlaps two lateral petals, which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals. This aestivation is
explanation: Standard overlaps wings, wings overlap the keel: vexillary or papilionaceous aestivation.
trap: Trap (A): Thinking petals merely touch at the margins | Trap (B): Assuming a regular one-over-next overlap as in china rose | Trap (D): Using the general term for irregular overlap seen in Cassia and gulmohur

question: Bulliform cells of grass leaves are modified
option_A: Adaxial epidermal cells along the veins
explanation: Certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins become large, empty and colourless bulliform cells; when flaccid they make the leaf curl inwards to reduce water loss.
trap: Trap (B): Assuming large colourless cells must be mesophyll derivatives | Trap (C): Confusing them with the large bundle sheath cells of grasses | Trap (D): Placing them on the lower epidermis

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. In dicot roots, pericycle cells initiate lateral roots and vascular cambium during secondary growth. II. Monocot stems have a sclerenchymatous hypodermis and water-containing cavities in the vascular bundles. III. Casparian strips are present in pericycle cells. IV. In a dorsiventral leaf, stomata are more abundant on the adaxial epidermis. V. Monocot roots usually have two to four xylem bundles.
explanation: I and II are correct. Casparian strips are endodermal; abaxial epidermis has more stomata; monocot roots are polyarch (usually more than six xylem bundles).
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement III, misplacing suberin strips of the endodermis in the pericycle | Trap (C): Also accepting III and IV, forgetting the abaxial surface bears more stomata | Trap (D): Accepting all, including the dicot xylem bundle number for monocot roots

question: The fruit of mango and coconut is a
explanation: Both are drupes developing from monocarpellary superior ovaries; mango has a fleshy mesocarp, coconut a fibrous one.
trap: Trap (A): Calling any fleshy fruit a berry | Trap (B): Confusing with the false fruit of apple | Trap (D): Thinking a fibrous coconut is a dry dehiscent fruit

question: Which floral description fits the family Solanaceae?
option_A: Stamens six in two whorls; ovary tricarpellary, syncarpous
option_B: Stamens five, epipetalous; ovary bicarpellary, syncarpous, superior
option_D: Stamens five, free from petals; ovary inferior, bicarpellary
explanation: Solanaceae: five epipetalous stamens; bicarpellary, syncarpous, superior ovary with swollen placenta and many ovules.
trap: Trap (A): Recalling the floral plan of a lily-type monocot flower | Trap (C): Recalling the pea-family flower with diadelphous stamens | Trap (D): Remembering five stamens but missing epipetaly and the superior ovary
review_note: Faculty flag: Solanaceae floral plan is in rationalised NCERT, but the NMC NEET UG 2026 family list names Malvaceae, Cruciferae, Leguminosae, Compositae and Gramineae.

question: Assertion (A): Mitochondria and chloroplasts are components of the endomembrane system. Reason (R): The functions of endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles are coordinated.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: The endomembrane system includes ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles because their functions are coordinated. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not part of it.
trap: Trap (A): Assuming every membrane-bound organelle belongs to the endomembrane system | Trap (B): Accepting the assertion and only doubting the link between the two | Trap (C): Accepting the assertion and doubting that ER and Golgi functions are coordinated

question: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and appearance of X-shaped chiasmata mark
explanation: Synapsis occurs in zygotene, crossing over in pachytene; in diplotene the complex dissolves and homologues separate except at chiasmata; diakinesis shows terminalisation.
trap: Trap (A): Linking chiasmata to the stage where crossing over occurs | Trap (C): Linking the synaptonemal complex to the stage where it forms | Trap (D): Confusing appearance of chiasmata with their terminalisation

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. During S phase the DNA content doubles but the chromosome number does not change. II. Centrioles duplicate during the G2 phase. III. Cells in the G0 stage are metabolically inactive. IV. Interphase lasts for less than 5 per cent of the cell cycle.
explanation: Only I is correct. Centrioles duplicate in S phase, G0 cells remain metabolically active, and interphase occupies more than 95 per cent of the cycle.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement II, shifting centriole duplication from S phase to G2 | Trap (C): Also accepting II and III, equating quiescent with metabolically inactive | Trap (D): Accepting all, reversing the proportion of interphase and M phase

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Golgi apparatus (b) Smooth ER (c) Lysosome (d) Contractile vacuole. Column II: (i) Osmoregulation in Amoeba (ii) Synthesis of steroidal hormones (iii) Hydrolases active at acidic pH (iv) Formation of glycolipids.
explanation: Golgi – glycoproteins and glycolipids; SER – lipid and steroid synthesis; lysosome – acid hydrolases; contractile vacuole – osmoregulation and excretion in Amoeba.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping lipid-related roles of Golgi and SER | Trap (B): Swapping lysosome and contractile vacuole, treating both as vacuolar bodies | Trap (C): Assigning hydrolases to Golgi because lysosomes are formed there

question: 70S ribosomes occur in
explanation: Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S; mitochondria and chloroplasts of eukaryotes also carry 70S ribosomes, while the cytoplasm has 80S.
trap: Trap (A): Assigning the smaller ribosome to the eukaryotic cytoplasm, which has 80S | Trap (B): Thinking bound ribosomes differ in size from free ones | Trap (D): Confusing the site of rRNA synthesis with the location of 70S ribosomes

question: A chromosome whose centromere lies close to one end, giving one extremely short and one very long arm, is
explanation: Acrocentric: centromere close to the end. Telocentric has a terminal centromere; sub-metacentric is slightly off-centre.
trap: Trap (A): Thinking a slightly off-centre centromere gives an extremely short arm | Trap (C): Confusing close to the end with exactly terminal | Trap (D): Ignoring arm-length difference altogether

question: Inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate is
option_B: Feedback inhibition by the end product
option_C: Non-competitive, because malonate binds away from the active site
option_D: Competitive, because malonate closely resembles succinate
explanation: An inhibitor closely resembling the substrate competes for the active site: competitive inhibition. Malonate resembles succinate.
trap: Trap (A): Mixing up regulation at a second site with inhibition by a substrate analogue | Trap (B): Treating malonate as a product of the pathway | Trap (C): Knowing it is inhibition but missing that the inhibitor competes for the substrate-binding site

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Cellulose is a homopolymer of glucose. II. Inulin is a polymer of fructose. III. Chitin is a complex polysaccharide in the exoskeleton of arthropods. IV. Glycogen is the storage polysaccharide of animals.
explanation: All four are correct as given in NCERT.
trap: Trap (B): Rejecting statement II, assuming every polysaccharide is made of glucose | Trap (C): Rejecting II and III, taking chitin to be a protein | Trap (D): Accepting only the familiar glycogen statement

question: In C4 plants the enzyme RuBisCO is located in
option_B: Both mesophyll and bundle sheath cells
explanation: Mesophyll cells of C4 plants lack RuBisCO and fix CO2 by PEP carboxylase; the Calvin cycle runs in bundle sheath cells, which are rich in RuBisCO but lack PEPcase.
trap: Trap (A): Placing RuBisCO where primary CO2 fixation occurs | Trap (B): Assuming every green cell has RuBisCO as in C3 plants | Trap (D): Confusing guard-cell-bearing epidermis with photosynthetic tissue

question: Assertion (A): Cyclic photophosphorylation yields ATP but not NADPH + H+. Reason (R): Both PS I and PS II are functional during cyclic photophosphorylation.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: Only PS I works in the cyclic flow; electrons return to PS I, so ATP is formed but neither NADPH nor O2.
trap: Trap (A): Assuming both photosystems always work together | Trap (B): Accepting the reason as a true but unrelated fact | Trap (D): Believing any light reaction must produce NADPH

question: To fix six molecules of CO2 through the Calvin cycle, a plant needs
explanation: Each CO2 needs 3 ATP and 2 NADPH; six turns need 18 ATP and 12 NADPH for one glucose.
trap: Trap (B): Reversing the ATP and NADPH numbers | Trap (C): Using the total ATP requirement of the C4 pathway | Trap (D): Giving the requirement for a single CO2

question: The net gain of ATP formed directly in glycolysis per glucose molecule is
explanation: Four ATP are formed and two are consumed, so the direct net gain is 2 ATP.
trap: Trap (A): Adding ATP expected from NADH oxidation | Trap (B): Counting ATP formed without subtracting the two used | Trap (C): Giving the total yield of aerobic respiration

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. The RQ of tripalmitin is about 0.7. II. Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate occurs in the mitochondrial matrix. III. Complex IV of the ETS is the cytochrome bc1 complex. IV. Fermentation releases more than half of the energy of glucose.
explanation: I and II are correct. Cytochrome bc1 is complex III (complex IV is cytochrome c oxidase); fermentation releases less than 7 per cent of the energy.
trap: Trap (A): Rejecting statement II, placing the pyruvate dehydrogenase step in the cytosol | Trap (C): Also accepting statement III, confusing complex III with complex IV | Trap (D): Accepting all, overlooking that fermentation releases less than seven per cent of the energy

question: Which plant growth regulator is used to speed up the malting process in brewing?
explanation: GA3 speeds malting; gibberellins also increase sugarcane stem length and delay senescence of fruits.
trap: Trap (A): Associating any industrial ripening-type use with ethylene | Trap (B): Linking nutrient mobilisation to cytokinin | Trap (C): Choosing the most widely used horticultural regulator

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Auxin (b) Cytokinin (c) Ethylene (d) Abscisic acid. Column II: (i) Closure of stomata (ii) Apical dominance (iii) Overcoming apical dominance (iv) Promotes root hair formation.
explanation: Auxin causes apical dominance; cytokinin overcomes it; ethylene promotes root growth and root hair formation; ABA closes stomata.
trap: Trap (A): Reversing which hormone causes and which overcomes apical dominance | Trap (C): Assigning root hair formation to cytokinin | Trap (D): Assigning root effects to auxin and apical dominance to ethylene

question: Formation of interfascicular cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is an example of
explanation: Living differentiated cells regaining the capacity to divide is dedifferentiation; products of such meristems later redifferentiate.
trap: Trap (A): Using the general term for maturation of meristem-derived cells | Trap (B): Confusing regaining of division capacity with the later loss of it | Trap (D): Confusing with environment-dependent change of form

question: During the light reaction in chloroplasts, protons accumulate in the
option_C: Intermembrane space of the chloroplast envelope
explanation: Water splitting, the proton-carrying electron transport and NADP+ reduction on the stroma side build a proton gradient with protons accumulating in the thylakoid lumen.
trap: Trap (B): Placing protons where ATP and NADPH are finally released | Trap (C): Transferring the mitochondrial location to the chloroplast | Trap (D): Using a mitochondrial compartment name

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. In over 60 per cent of angiosperms pollen grains are shed at the 2-celled stage. II. A typical embryo sac is 7-celled and 8-nucleate at maturity. III. Tapetum is the outermost wall layer of the microsporangium. IV. Sporopollenin is the main component of the intine. V. The filiform apparatus is present in the antipodal cells.
explanation: I and II are correct. Tapetum is the innermost wall layer, sporopollenin forms the exine, and the filiform apparatus is in synergids.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement IV, mixing up exine and intine | Trap (C): Also accepting III and IV, placing tapetum outside instead of innermost | Trap (D): Accepting all, including the filiform apparatus that belongs to synergids

question: Transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant is
explanation: Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination but genetically similar to autogamy.
trap: Trap (A): Thinking same plant means same flower | Trap (B): Thinking a different flower always means a different plant | Trap (D): Confusing a type of flower with a type of pollination

question: Assertion (A): Endosperm development precedes embryo development. Reason (R): The primary endosperm nucleus is triploid in most angiosperms.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: Both are true, but endosperm forms first to assure nutrition for the developing embryo; triploidy does not explain the order.
trap: Trap (A): Assuming any true fact about endosperm explains the timing | Trap (C): Doubting triploidy of the primary endosperm nucleus | Trap (D): Believing the zygote divides before the primary endosperm cell

question: Perisperm, the residual persistent nucellus, is found in
explanation: In black pepper and beet remnants of nucellus persist as perisperm.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing persistent endosperm with perisperm | Trap (B): Confusing cereal endosperm with nucellus | Trap (C): Choosing non-albuminous seeds where nothing persists

question: In Citrus and mango, some nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac divide, protrude into it and form embryos. This results in
explanation: Occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed is polyembryony; here the extra embryos are apomictic nucellar embryos.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing fertilisation-free embryo formation with seedless fruit formation | Trap (C): Assuming extra embryos need extra fertilisation events | Trap (D): Linking non-ovarian tissue with false fruit

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Water hyacinth and water lily are pollinated by water. II. In Vallisneria pollination takes place on the water surface. III. Wind-pollinated flowers produce sticky pollen and large colourful petals. IV. Yucca is pollinated by a species of wasp.
explanation: Only II is correct. Water hyacinth and water lily are pollinated by insects or wind; wind-pollinated pollen is light and non-sticky; Yucca is pollinated by a moth.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement I, assuming all aquatic plants use water | Trap (C): Also accepting I and IV, confusing the Yucca moth with the fig wasp | Trap (D): Accepting all, including insect-flower traits for wind pollination

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Frederick Griffith (b) Meselson and Stahl (c) Jacob and Monod (d) Alec Jeffreys. Column II: (i) DNA fingerprinting (ii) Transforming principle (iii) Lac operon (iv) Semiconservative replication.
explanation: Griffith – transformation; Meselson and Stahl – semiconservative replication; Jacob and Monod – lac operon; Jeffreys – DNA fingerprinting.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping the two classic bacterial experiments | Trap (B): Swapping operon and replication discoveries | Trap (C): Swapping the lac operon and DNA fingerprinting

question: A plant heterozygous for two independently assorting genes is crossed with a double recessive plant. The phenotypic ratio in the progeny is
explanation: The heterozygote forms four gamete types in equal proportion; with a recessive tester these give four phenotypes in 1:1:1:1.
trap: Trap (A): Applying the F2 dihybrid ratio to a test cross | Trap (B): Applying the monohybrid F2 ratio | Trap (D): Applying the monohybrid genotypic ratio

question: The number of genotypes possible for the ABO blood groups in humans is
explanation: Three alleles (IA, IB, i) give six genotypes and four phenotypes.
trap: Trap (A): Counting alleles instead of genotypes | Trap (C): Counting phenotypes instead of genotypes | Trap (D): Squaring the number of alleles without removing duplicates

question: In Morgan's work on Drosophila, the recombination frequency between the genes for white eye and miniature wing was
explanation: Yellow and white were tightly linked (1.3 per cent recombination); white and miniature showed 37.2 per cent recombination.
trap: Trap (A): Recalling the value for the tightly linked yellow and white genes | Trap (B): Recalling the parental-type percentage of the yellow-white cross | Trap (C): Recalling the parental-type percentage of the white-miniature cross

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. RNA polymerase III transcribes hnRNA. II. UTRs are present at both the 5' and 3' ends of mRNA and are required for efficient translation. III. During tailing, methyl guanosine triphosphate is added to the 3' end of hnRNA. IV. In bacteria the sigma factor terminates transcription.
explanation: Only II is correct. RNA polymerase II makes hnRNA; capping adds methyl guanosine triphosphate at the 5' end and tailing adds adenylate residues at the 3' end; rho terminates.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement IV, confusing sigma (initiation) with rho (termination) | Trap (C): Also accepting III and IV, mixing capping with tailing | Trap (D): Accepting all, including the wrong polymerase for hnRNA

question: Which human chromosome carries the largest number of genes?
explanation: Chromosome 1 has the most genes (2968) and Y the fewest (231).
trap: Trap (A): Assuming the sex chromosome with many known disorders has most genes | Trap (B): Reversing the fact: Y has the fewest genes | Trap (D): Associating a well-known trisomy chromosome with gene richness

question: A colour-blind man marries a woman who is homozygous for normal vision. The probability that their son is colour-blind is
explanation: Sons receive the Y from the father and a normal X from the mother, so none is colour-blind; all daughters are carriers.
trap: Trap (A): Treating the trait as autosomal with half the children affected | Trap (B): Applying a 3:1 type calculation | Trap (D): Assuming sons inherit the X-linked trait from the father

question: Assertion (A): In sickle-cell anaemia, valine replaces glutamic acid at the sixth position of the beta-globin chain. Reason (R): A single base substitution changes the sixth codon of the beta-globin gene from GAG to GUG.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: GAG codes for glutamic acid and GUG for valine, so the point mutation directly causes the amino acid replacement.
trap: Trap (B): Treating the codon change and amino acid change as unrelated facts | Trap (C): Believing the mutation is a frame-shift rather than a substitution | Trap (D): Reversing the amino acids involved

question: Which ecological pyramid can never be inverted?
explanation: Energy is lost as heat at each transfer, so the pyramid of energy is always upright.
trap: Trap (A): Generalising from the grassland ecosystem | Trap (B): Forgetting the inverted biomass pyramid of the sea | Trap (C): Assuming all pyramids are upright in all ecosystems

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Cuscuta growing on hedge plants is a parasite. II. Barnacles growing on the back of a whale show commensalism. III. Cattle egrets foraging near grazing cattle show mutualism. IV. The Abingdon tortoise became extinct on the Galapagos because of predation by goats.
explanation: I and II are correct. Egret-cattle is commensalism; the tortoise went extinct due to competition from goats.
trap: Trap (A): Rejecting statement II, assuming the whale is harmed | Trap (C): Also accepting statement III, assuming cattle also benefit | Trap (D): Accepting all, although goats outcompeted the tortoise by browsing

question: For frugivorous birds and mammals in the tropical forests of different continents, the slope of the species-area regression line is
explanation: Z is 0.1 to 0.2 for most regions, 0.6 to 1.2 for very large areas such as continents; the value for frugivorous birds and mammals is 1.15.
trap: Trap (A): Using the lower limit of Z for small regional areas | Trap (B): Using the upper limit of Z for small regional areas | Trap (C): Using the lower limit for whole continents instead of the specific value

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Dodo (b) Quagga (c) Thylacine (d) Steller's sea cow. Column II: (i) Australia (ii) Russia (iii) Mauritius (iv) Africa.
explanation: Dodo – Mauritius; quagga – Africa; thylacine – Australia; Steller's sea cow – Russia.
trap: Trap (A): Placing the dodo on the African mainland | Trap (C): Swapping quagga and thylacine | Trap (D): Swapping thylacine and Steller's sea cow
review_note: Faculty flag: Match item shares its option codes and key (B) with P1-010 and P2-110 (template similarity 0.85; different facts).

question: The file-like rasping organ called radula is found in
explanation: The mouth of molluscs contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, the radula.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing it with the mouth parts of insects | Trap (B): Confusing with jaws of Nereis | Trap (D): Confusing with the feeding apparatus of sea urchins

question: A worm-like marine animal with an open circulatory system, respiration by gills and excretion through a proboscis gland is
explanation: Hemichordates such as Balanoglossus and Saccoglossus have a proboscis gland as the excretory organ and an open circulatory system.
trap: Trap (B): Choosing a worm-like annelid that has closed circulation and nephridia | Trap (C): Confusing hemichordates with urochordates | Trap (D): Choosing an echinoderm, which lacks an excretory system

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. In cyclostomes the cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous. II. Cartilaginous fishes lack an air bladder and must swim constantly. III. In bony fishes the gills are not covered by an operculum. IV. The amphibian heart is two-chambered. V. All mammals are viviparous.
explanation: I and II are correct. Bony fishes have an operculum on each side, amphibians have a three-chambered heart, and Ornithorhynchus is oviparous.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement V, forgetting the egg-laying platypus | Trap (C): Also accepting IV and V, giving the fish heart to amphibians | Trap (D): Accepting all, including reversal of the operculum fact

question: Flame cells that help in osmoregulation and excretion are found in
explanation: Flatworms have specialised flame cells for osmoregulation and excretion.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing the two helminth phyla | Trap (B): Confusing with nephridia | Trap (D): Assuming simple animals with a gastrovascular cavity have flame cells

question: Which statement about the frog is correct?
option_A: In females the ureters and oviducts open by a common duct into the cloaca
option_B: In males the ureters act as urinogenital ducts opening into the cloaca
option_D: Mature RBCs of the frog lack a nucleus
explanation: In male frogs the ureters carry both urine and sperm; in females ureters and oviducts open separately. Frogs are ureotelic and have nucleated RBCs.
trap: Trap (A): Extending the male arrangement to females | Trap (C): Assuming a land-visiting animal must be uricotelic | Trap (D): Transferring the mammalian RBC feature to frogs

question: Assertion (A): Aschelminthes are acoelomate animals. Reason (R): In Aschelminthes the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: A body cavity not lined by mesoderm, with mesoderm as scattered pouches, is a pseudocoelom. Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates; Platyhelminthes are acoelomates.
trap: Trap (A): Reading scattered mesoderm as no body cavity at all | Trap (B): Accepting the assertion and merely doubting the causal link | Trap (C): Accepting the assertion and assuming mesoderm lines the cavity fully

question: Tendons, in which collagen fibres lie in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres, are made of
explanation: Parallel orientation of fibres defines dense regular connective tissue, as in tendons and ligaments.
trap: Trap (A): Ignoring the orientation of fibres; this type occurs in skin | Trap (C): Choosing the commonest loose connective tissue | Trap (D): Choosing another loose connective tissue specialised for fat storage

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue. II. Gap junctions connect the cytoplasm of adjoining cells. III. Ciliated epithelium lines bronchioles and fallopian tubes. IV. Compound epithelium has a limited role in secretion and absorption.
explanation: All four are correct. Compound epithelium is mainly protective.
trap: Trap (B): Rejecting statement IV, assuming all epithelia are equally secretory | Trap (C): Rejecting two statements by mixing up tight and gap junctions | Trap (D): Accepting only the ciliated epithelium statement

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Tidal volume (b) Inspiratory reserve volume (c) Expiratory reserve volume (d) Residual volume. Column II: (i) 1100–1200 mL (ii) 2500–3000 mL (iii) 1000–1100 mL (iv) about 500 mL.
explanation: TV about 500 mL; IRV 2500–3000 mL; ERV 1000–1100 mL; RV 1100–1200 mL.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping the close values of ERV and RV | Trap (B): Swapping IRV and ERV | Trap (C): Giving the largest value to tidal volume

question: About 70 per cent of carbon dioxide is transported in blood as
explanation: Nearly 70 per cent of CO2 travels as bicarbonate, 20–25 per cent as carbamino-haemoglobin and about 7 per cent dissolved in plasma.
trap: Trap (A): Overestimating the 20–25 per cent carried by haemoglobin | Trap (B): Overestimating the 7 per cent dissolved in plasma | Trap (D): Confusing the CO compound of haemoglobin with CO2 transport

question: The pneumotaxic centre, which can moderate the respiratory rhythm centre, is located in the
explanation: The rhythm centre lies in the medulla; the pneumotaxic centre in the pons can reduce the duration of inspiration.
trap: Trap (A): Placing it with the respiratory rhythm centre | Trap (C): Assuming the hypothalamus controls all involuntary functions | Trap (D): Confusing a peripheral chemoreceptor site with a brain centre

question: A trained athlete has a stroke volume of 100 mL and a heart rate of 60 beats per minute. The cardiac output is
explanation: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate = 100 × 60 = 6000 mL per minute.
trap: Trap (A): Quoting the memorised average value instead of calculating | Trap (B): Dividing stroke volume by heart rate | Trap (C): Adding stroke volume and heart rate

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. The P-wave represents depolarisation of the atria. II. The QRS complex represents repolarisation of the ventricles. III. The T-wave represents repolarisation of the atria. IV. The end of the T-wave marks the beginning of ventricular systole.
explanation: Only I is correct. QRS is ventricular depolarisation, T-wave is ventricular repolarisation and its end marks the end of systole.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement IV, reversing the start and end of systole | Trap (C): Also accepting III and IV, assigning the T-wave to atria | Trap (D): Accepting all, including QRS as repolarisation

question: The plasma protein mainly responsible for maintaining osmotic balance is
explanation: Fibrinogens are needed for clotting, globulins for defence, albumins for osmotic balance.
trap: Trap (A): Choosing the clotting protein | Trap (B): Choosing the defence protein | Trap (D): Choosing another clotting factor

question: Assertion (A): The sino-atrial node is called the pacemaker of the heart. Reason (R): Among nodal tissues, the SA node generates the minimum number of action potentials per minute.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: The SAN generates the maximum number of action potentials (70–75 per minute) and so initiates and maintains the rhythm.
trap: Trap (A): Missing the word minimum and reading the reason as the usual explanation | Trap (B): Treating the reason as a true but separate fact | Trap (D): Believing the AV node sets the rhythm

question: With a glomerular filtration rate of about 125 mL per minute, the volume of filtrate formed by the kidneys per day is about
explanation: 125 mL per minute equals about 180 litres per day; nearly 99 per cent is reabsorbed, giving about 1.5 litres of urine.
trap: Trap (B): Giving the daily urine output instead of filtrate | Trap (C): Reading the per-minute figure as litres per day | Trap (D): Using the renal blood flow figure of 1100–1200 mL per minute

question: The osmolarity of the interstitial fluid in the inner medulla of the human kidney is about
explanation: The gradient rises from about 300 mOsmol per litre in the cortex to about 1200 in the inner medulla.
trap: Trap (A): Giving the value for the cortex | Trap (B): Giving an intermediate medullary value | Trap (C): Giving an intermediate value, underestimating the gradient

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. ADH facilitates water reabsorption from the latter parts of the tubule. II. ANF causes vasodilation and thereby decreases blood pressure. III. Renin converts angiotensin I into angiotensin II. IV. Aldosterone promotes reabsorption of K+ and water from the distal parts of the tubule.
explanation: I, II and III are correct. NCERT states that renin converts angiotensinogen in blood to angiotensin I and further to angiotensin II. ANF causes vasodilation and thereby decreases blood pressure. Aldosterone causes reabsorption of Na+ and water, not K+, from the distal tubule.
trap: Trap (A): Counting only statement I and rejecting ANF as opposing RAAS | Trap (B): Rejecting statement III by invoking ACE, although NCERT attributes conversion of angiotensinogen to angiotensin I and further to angiotensin II to renin | Trap (D): Also accepting statement IV, confusing Na+ reabsorption with K+
review_note: Faculty flag: Renin/ACE item keyed to NCERT wording rather than physiology texts.

question: During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, which of the following retains its length?
explanation: Thin filaments slide over thick ones: I-bands and H-zone reduce and the sarcomere shortens, but the A-band retains its length.
trap: Trap (A): Assuming the light band is unaffected | Trap (B): Assuming the central zone of thick filaments is fixed | Trap (C): Thinking filaments slide without shortening the sarcomere

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Ball and socket joint (b) Hinge joint (c) Pivot joint (d) Saddle joint. Column II: (i) Between carpal and metacarpal of thumb (ii) Between humerus and pectoral girdle (iii) Knee joint (iv) Between atlas and axis.
explanation: Ball and socket – humerus and pectoral girdle; hinge – knee; pivot – atlas and axis; saddle – carpal and metacarpal of thumb.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping ball and socket with hinge | Trap (C): Swapping pivot and saddle | Trap (D): Swapping hinge and pivot

question: The number of cranial bones in the human skull is
explanation: The skull has 8 cranial and 14 facial bones, 22 in all.
trap: Trap (A): Giving the number of facial bones | Trap (B): Giving cranial plus facial bones | Trap (D): Confusing with pairs of ribs

question: The sodium-potassium pump of the axonal membrane transports
option_A: 3 Na+ outwards for 2 K+ into the cell
option_B: 2 Na+ outwards for 3 K+ into the cell
option_C: 3 Na+ into the cell for 2 K+ outwards
option_D: 3 K+ outwards for 2 Na+ into the cell
explanation: The pump moves 3 Na+ out for 2 K+ in, helping maintain the resting potential.
trap: Trap (B): Reversing the numbers | Trap (C): Reversing the directions | Trap (D): Reversing both ions and directions

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Unipolar neurons are usually found in the embryonic stage. II. Impulse transmission across an electrical synapse is faster than across a chemical synapse. III. Schwann cells are absent around unmyelinated nerve fibres. IV. At rest the axonal membrane is more permeable to Na+ than to K+. V. The corpus callosum connects the cerebrum with the cerebellum.
explanation: I and II are correct. Unmyelinated fibres are enclosed by Schwann cells that do not form myelin; the resting membrane is more permeable to K+; the corpus callosum joins the two cerebral hemispheres.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement III, equating no myelin with no Schwann cell | Trap (C): Also accepting III and IV, reversing resting permeability | Trap (D): Accepting all, including the wrong connection for the corpus callosum

question: The hormone that regulates the 24-hour diurnal rhythm of the body is
explanation: Melatonin from the pineal gland regulates the sleep-wake cycle, body temperature and other rhythms.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing pineal with thymus | Trap (B): Linking metabolic rate with the body clock | Trap (D): Linking stress response with daily rhythm

question: Assertion (A): Glucagon is a hyperglycemic hormone. Reason (R): Glucagon is a peptide hormone secreted by the alpha-cells of the islets of Langerhans.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: Both are true, but glucagon raises blood sugar because it stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, not because of its chemical nature or source.
trap: Trap (A): Assuming a true statement about the same hormone must be the explanation | Trap (C): Assigning glucagon to beta-cells or calling it a steroid | Trap (D): Mixing up the actions of insulin and glucagon

question: Which hormone acts through intracellular receptors and regulates gene expression?
explanation: Steroid hormones and iodothyronines act through intracellular receptors; peptide hormones and catecholamines use membrane-bound receptors and second messengers.
trap: Trap (A): Assuming a hormone affecting many tissues must enter cells | Trap (B): Treating all pancreatic hormones as gene regulators | Trap (C): Assuming a fast-acting hormone works inside the nucleus

question: The second meiotic division of the secondary oocyte is completed
option_A: Just before ovulation in the Graafian follicle
option_B: Only when a sperm enters the oocyte
option_C: At puberty in all primary oocytes
explanation: Entry of sperm induces completion of meiosis II, forming the ootid and second polar body.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing completion of meiosis I with meiosis II | Trap (C): Confusing resumption of meiosis I at puberty with completion of meiosis II | Trap (D): Assuming meiosis ends late in embryonic development

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Leydig cells lie in the interstitial spaces and secrete androgens. II. Sertoli cells secrete testosterone. III. Each testis contains about 250 seminiferous tubules. IV. The scrotum keeps the testes 2–2.5 °C warmer than the body.
explanation: Only I is correct. Sertoli cells nourish germ cells; each testis has about 250 lobules, each with one to three tubules; the scrotum keeps the testes 2–2.5 °C cooler.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement III, confusing testicular lobules with tubules | Trap (C): Also accepting II and III, mixing up Sertoli and Leydig cells | Trap (D): Accepting all, reversing the temperature difference

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Multiload 375 (b) LNG-20 (c) Lippes loop (d) Saheli. Column II: (i) Non-medicated IUD (ii) Copper-releasing IUD (iii) Non-steroidal oral pill (iv) Hormone-releasing IUD.
explanation: Multiload 375 – copper-releasing; LNG-20 – hormone-releasing; Lippes loop – non-medicated; Saheli – non-steroidal once-a-week pill.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping copper-releasing and hormone-releasing IUDs | Trap (B): Swapping LNG-20 and Lippes loop | Trap (C): Swapping Multiload and Lippes loop

question: The LH surge in the middle of the menstrual cycle induces
explanation: Rapid LH secretion at mid-cycle causes rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum.
trap: Trap (A): Linking any hormonal change to bleeding | Trap (B): Confusing with a post-fertilisation event | Trap (D): Confusing LH with oxytocin-driven labour

question: In ZIFT, the zygote or an early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres is transferred into the
explanation: ZIFT places the zygote or early embryo in the fallopian tube; embryos with more than 8 blastomeres go into the uterus.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing with IUT, used for embryos with more than 8 blastomeres | Trap (C): Confusing with the site of artificial insemination | Trap (D): Assuming the embryo is returned to where the ovum came from

question: The first movements of the foetus and the appearance of hair on its head are usually observed during the
explanation: Heart forms after one month; limbs and digits by the second month; most organ systems by 12 weeks; first movements and head hair in the fifth month.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing with formation of the heart | Trap (B): Confusing with formation of limbs and external genital organs | Trap (C): Confusing with fine body hair, eyelid separation and eyelashes

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Lactational amenorrhea is effective only up to a maximum of six months after parturition. II. Hepatitis-B and HIV can spread by sharing injection needles. III. Amniocentesis uses foetal cells and dissolved substances of the amniotic fluid. IV. In vasectomy a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up.
explanation: All four statements are correct.
trap: Trap (B): Rejecting statement I, thinking the method works throughout lactation | Trap (C): Rejecting two statements by treating these infections as purely sexually transmitted | Trap (D): Accepting only the vasectomy statement

question: Which of the following is an example of analogous structures?
option_B: Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
option_C: Eye of octopus and eye of mammals
explanation: Analogous organs are not anatomically similar but perform similar functions, a result of convergent evolution.
trap: Trap (A): Judging by different function while the bone pattern is the same | Trap (B): Judging by different appearance though both are modified branches | Trap (D): Missing common ancestry of vertebrate organs

question: In a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 16 per cent of individuals show the recessive phenotype. The frequency of heterozygotes is
trap: Trap (A): Giving the homozygous dominant frequency | Trap (B): Calculating pq and forgetting to double it | Trap (D): Giving all individuals with the dominant phenotype

question: Assertion (A): Australian marsupials are an example of adaptive radiation. Reason (R): A number of marsupials, each different from the others, evolved from an ancestral stock within the Australian island continent.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: Evolution of different forms from a common point within one geographical area, radiating to different habitats, is adaptive radiation.
trap: Trap (B): Not recognising that the reason is the definition applied to this case | Trap (C): Believing marsupials migrated in as already distinct forms | Trap (D): Treating the case as convergent evolution only

question: Which hominid had a brain capacity of about 900 cc and probably ate meat?
explanation: Homo erectus, about 1.5 mya, had a brain of around 900 cc and probably ate meat.
trap: Trap (A): Choosing the fruit-eating hunter with stone weapons | Trap (B): Choosing the 650–800 cc form that probably did not eat meat | Trap (C): Choosing the 1400 cc form that buried its dead

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Miller's experiment used CH4, H2, NH3 and water vapour at 800 °C. II. According to de Vries, mutations are random and directionless. III. After industrialisation in England, white-winged moths became predominant. IV. The founder effect is produced by natural selection.
explanation: I and II are correct. Dark-winged moths predominated after industrialisation; the founder effect results from genetic drift.
trap: Trap (A): Rejecting statement II, assigning directional variation to de Vries | Trap (C): Also accepting statement III, reversing industrial melanism | Trap (D): Accepting all, treating founder effect as selection rather than drift
concept: Evolution – Origin of life and mechanisms

question: Haemozoin, the toxic substance responsible for the chill and high fever of malaria, is released when
option_B: Sporozoites collect in the mosquito's salivary glands
option_C: Gametocytes fuse in the mosquito's gut
explanation: Parasites multiply in RBCs; their rupture releases haemozoin, causing chill and high fever recurring every three to four days.
trap: Trap (A): Linking symptoms to the first site of multiplication | Trap (B): Linking symptoms to the infective stage | Trap (C): Confusing events in the mosquito with events in humans

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Typhoid (b) Pneumonia (c) Filariasis (d) Ringworm. Column II: (i) Haemophilus influenzae (ii) Wuchereria malayi (iii) Microsporum (iv) Salmonella typhi.
explanation: Typhoid – Salmonella typhi; pneumonia – Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae; filariasis – Wuchereria; ringworm – Microsporum, Trichophyton, Epidermophyton.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping the two bacterial pathogens | Trap (C): Assuming ringworm is caused by a worm | Trap (D): Swapping the pneumonia and filariasis agents

question: The antibody abundant in colostrum that protects the newborn is
explanation: Colostrum has abundant IgA; the foetus receives IgG through the placenta.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing with the antibody that crosses the placenta | Trap (B): Confusing with the antibody of allergic reactions | Trap (D): Choosing the first antibody of a primary response

question: Cocaine interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter
explanation: Cocaine, from Erythroxylum coca, interferes with dopamine transport and strongly stimulates the CNS.
trap: Trap (B): Choosing the best-known neuromuscular transmitter | Trap (C): Confusing with depressant-type drug action | Trap (D): Confusing with mood-related drugs such as LSD-type hallucinogens

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. HIV is a retrovirus with an RNA genome. II. Infected macrophages act like an HIV factory. III. Benign tumours show metastasis. IV. Thymus and bone marrow are secondary lymphoid organs. V. Injecting antivenom after snakebite is active immunisation.
explanation: I and II are correct. Metastasis is a property of malignant tumours; thymus and bone marrow are primary lymphoid organs; antivenom gives passive immunity.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement V, confusing preformed antibodies with vaccination | Trap (C): Also accepting IV and V, mixing primary and secondary lymphoid organs | Trap (D): Accepting all, including metastasis for benign tumours

question: The enzyme that joins cut DNA fragments by sealing their ends is
explanation: DNA ligase links sticky ends produced by the same restriction enzyme to form recombinant DNA.
trap: Trap (A): Thinking synthesis and joining are the same | Trap (B): Confusing molecular scissors with the molecular glue | Trap (D): Choosing an enzyme that removes nucleotides from ends

question: A foreign gene is ligated at the BamHI site of pBR322. Bacteria carrying this recombinant plasmid will
option_A: Grow on tetracycline but not on ampicillin
option_B: Grow on ampicillin but not on tetracycline
explanation: BamHI lies in the tetracycline resistance gene; insertion inactivates it while ampicillin resistance remains.
trap: Trap (A): Placing the BamHI site in the ampicillin resistance gene | Trap (C): Forgetting insertional inactivation | Trap (D): Confusing recombinants with non-transformants

question: Assertion (A): During gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move towards the cathode. Reason (R): DNA fragments are negatively charged molecules.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: Being negatively charged, DNA moves towards the anode through the agarose matrix; smaller fragments move farther.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing cathode with the positive electrode | Trap (B): Accepting the assertion and seeing charge as unrelated to movement | Trap (C): Accepting the assertion and assuming DNA is positively charged

question: The protein encoded by the gene cryIAb controls
explanation: cryIAc and cryIIAb control cotton bollworms; cryIAb controls corn borer.
trap: Trap (A): Confusing with cryIAc and cryIIAb | Trap (C): Confusing Bt toxin with the RNAi strategy | Trap (D): Assuming Bt toxin acts on all sap-sucking pests

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Taq polymerase is isolated from Thermus aquaticus. II. The denaturation step of PCR requires DNA ligase. III. Primers are small chemically synthesised polypeptides. IV. The stirrer in a stirred-tank bioreactor reduces oxygen availability.
explanation: Only I is correct. Denaturation uses heat; primers are oligonucleotides; the stirrer ensures even mixing and oxygen availability.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement III, confusing oligonucleotides with polypeptides | Trap (C): Also accepting II and III, assuming an enzyme separates strands in PCR | Trap (D): Accepting all, reversing the role of the stirrer

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Rosie, the transgenic cow (b) ADA deficiency (c) Eli Lilly, 1983 (d) RNA interference. Column II: (i) Nematode-resistant tobacco (ii) Human alpha-lactalbumin in milk (iii) First clinical gene therapy (iv) Insulin chains by rDNA technology.
explanation: Rosie – human alpha-lactalbumin enriched milk; ADA deficiency – first gene therapy (1990); Eli Lilly – insulin chains A and B; RNAi – protection against Meloidogyne incognita.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping the two protein products, milk protein and insulin | Trap (B): Swapping gene therapy and RNAi | Trap (C): Assigning gene therapy to Rosie

question: The extra stretch present in proinsulin but removed during maturation into insulin is the
explanation: Mature insulin has chains A and B linked by disulphide bridges; the C-peptide of the prohormone is removed.
trap: Trap (A): Naming a chain that is retained in mature insulin | Trap (B): Naming the other retained chain | Trap (D): Confusing the bonds joining the chains with a removed segment

question: Rhizopus, Mucor and Albugo are members of
explanation: Phycomycetes have aseptate, coenocytic mycelium; examples are Mucor, Rhizopus (bread mould) and Albugo (parasitic on mustard).
trap: Trap (A): Grouping all common moulds with Penicillium and Aspergillus | Trap (C): Confusing a parasitic fungus on mustard with rusts and smuts | Trap (D): Assuming moulds with only asexual spores seen in class belong to imperfect fungi

question: In mosses, the leafy stage of the gametophyte develops
option_B: From the zygote inside the archegonium
option_C: From gemmae formed in gemma cups
option_D: From the secondary protonema as a lateral bud
explanation: The moss gametophyte has two stages: the protonema, formed directly from a spore, and the leafy stage, which arises from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud.
trap: Trap (A): Skipping the protonema, which is the first stage formed from the spore | Trap (B): Confusing the gametophyte with the sporophyte, which arises from the zygote | Trap (C): Transferring the asexual buds of liverworts to mosses

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Viroids consist of low molecular weight RNA without a protein coat. II. Viruses that infect plants generally have double-stranded DNA. III. In a lichen the algal partner is called the mycobiont. IV. Bacteriophages usually have single-stranded RNA.
explanation: Only I is correct. Plant viruses generally have single-stranded RNA, bacteriophages usually have double-stranded DNA, and the algal partner of a lichen is the phycobiont.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement III, interchanging phycobiont and mycobiont | Trap (C): Also accepting II and III, giving plant viruses the genome of bacteriophages | Trap (D): Accepting all, including the wrong genome for bacteriophages

question: The characteristic colour of brown algae is due to the xanthophyll pigment
explanation: Brown algae contain chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls; their shade depends on the amount of fucoxanthin.
trap: Trap (A): Recalling the red pigment of Rhodophyceae | Trap (B): Recalling the accessory pigment of green algae | Trap (D): Recalling a pigment of cyanobacteria

question: The prothallus of a pteridophyte is best described as
option_A: A diploid sporophyte dependent on the gametophyte
option_B: A non-green structure parasitic on the sporophyte
option_C: A small, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte
option_D: The leafy stage that bears sporangia on sporophylls
explanation: Spores germinate into an inconspicuous, small but multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte called the prothallus.
trap: Trap (A): Carrying over the bryophyte pattern, where the sporophyte is the dependent phase | Trap (B): Carrying over the seed-plant pattern, where the gametophyte is retained on the sporophyte | Trap (D): Confusing the gametophyte with the dominant sporophyte

question: Assertion (A): Members of Rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae. Reason (R): The red pigment r-phycoerythrin predominates in their body.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: Red algae are so named because of the predominance of the red pigment r-phycoerythrin.
trap: Trap (B): Treating the pigment fact as unrelated to the name | Trap (C): Believing red algae lack phycoerythrin and owe the colour to carotenoids | Trap (D): Thinking the name refers to red tides, which are caused by dinoflagellates

question: Whorled phyllotaxy, with more than two leaves at each node, is seen in
explanation: Alternate: china rose, mustard, sunflower. Opposite: Calotropis, guava. Whorled: Alstonia.
trap: Trap (A): Choosing an example of alternate phyllotaxy | Trap (B): Choosing an example of opposite phyllotaxy | Trap (C): Choosing the other example of opposite phyllotaxy

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. In a hypogynous flower the ovary is superior. II. Plum, rose and peach have perigynous flowers. III. In an epigynous flower the ovary is superior. IV. Mustard has zygomorphic flowers.
explanation: I and II are correct. Epigynous flowers have an inferior ovary; mustard, datura and chilli are actinomorphic.
trap: Trap (A): Rejecting statement II, calling the half-inferior condition epigynous | Trap (C): Also accepting statement III, reversing superior and inferior | Trap (D): Accepting all, including bilateral symmetry for the actinomorphic mustard flower
concept: Morphology – Flower: position of ovary and symmetry

question: A student examines a transverse section of a plant organ and records: a sclerenchymatous hypodermis; many scattered vascular bundles, each with a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath; peripheral bundles smaller than the central ones; phloem parenchyma absent; no cambium; a large parenchymatous ground tissue not divided into cortex and pith. The organ is a
explanation: Scattered, conjoint, closed bundles with sclerenchymatous sheaths, a sclerenchymatous hypodermis and undifferentiated ground tissue identify a monocot stem.
trap: Trap (A): Ignoring that dicot stem bundles form a ring and are open | Trap (B): Ignoring that root bundles are radial, not conjoint and scattered | Trap (C): Ignoring both the scattered arrangement and the absence of radial bundles
concept: Anatomy – Identifying an organ from a transverse section

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Monadelphous stamens (b) Diadelphous stamens (c) Polyadelphous stamens (d) Epiphyllous stamens. Column II: (i) Citrus (ii) Lily (iii) China rose (iv) Pea.
explanation: Monadelphous – china rose; diadelphous – pea; polyadelphous – citrus; epiphyllous (attached to perianth) – lily.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping one-bundle and two-bundle conditions | Trap (C): Swapping pea and citrus | Trap (D): Swapping citrus and lily
review_note: Faculty flag: Match item shares its option codes and key (B) with P1-010 and P1-050 (template similarity 0.83; different facts).

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Guard cells of grasses are dumb-bell shaped. II. Trichomes of the shoot system are usually multicellular. III. Root hairs are unicellular elongations of epidermal cells. IV. Vascular bundles of the dicot stem are closed. V. The ground tissue of leaves is called pith.
explanation: I, II and III are correct. Dicot stem bundles are open; in leaves the ground tissue is the mesophyll.
trap: Trap (A): Accepting only the guard cell statement | Trap (B): Rejecting statement II, assuming trichomes are unicellular like root hairs | Trap (D): Also accepting statement IV, forgetting that cambium makes dicot stem bundles open

question: The single large, shield-shaped cotyledon of a maize grain is the
explanation: In monocot seeds the embryo has one large shield-shaped cotyledon, the scutellum.
trap: Trap (B): Confusing with the sheath enclosing the plumule | Trap (C): Confusing with the sheath enclosing the radicle | Trap (D): Confusing with the proteinous layer around the endosperm

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. In monocots the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots. II. The apex of the root is covered by a root cap. III. The pulvinus is a swollen leaf base found in some leguminous plants. IV. Neem has pinnately compound leaves.
explanation: All four statements are correct.
trap: Trap (B): Rejecting statement III, taking the pulvinus to be a stem structure | Trap (C): Rejecting two statements, including neem as a simple leaf | Trap (D): Accepting only the root cap statement

question: Vesicles budding from the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with which face of the Golgi apparatus?
option_A: Trans face, the convex maturing face
option_B: Cis face, the concave maturing face
option_C: Cis face, the convex forming face
option_D: Trans face, the concave forming face
explanation: The Golgi has a convex cis (forming) face and a concave trans (maturing) face; ER vesicles fuse with the cis face.
trap: Trap (A): Naming the exit face and giving it the wrong curvature | Trap (B): Getting cis right but attaching the description of the trans face | Trap (D): Getting the curvature of trans right but calling it the forming face

question: Assertion (A): Mitochondria divide by fission. Reason (R): The mitochondrial matrix possesses a single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules and 70S ribosomes.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: Both statements are true as given in NCERT, but the composition of the matrix is not offered as the explanation for fission.
trap: Trap (A): Assuming that possessing DNA is the stated cause of fission | Trap (C): Believing mitochondria have 80S ribosomes or linear DNA | Trap (D): Believing mitochondria are formed afresh by the ER

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. A yeast cell can complete its cell cycle in about 90 minutes. II. In animal cells cytokinesis takes place by cell plate formation. III. Centromeres split during anaphase I. IV. DNA replicates during interkinesis. V. Bivalents align on the equatorial plate in metaphase I.
explanation: I and V are correct. Animal cells divide by a furrow; in anaphase I homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids stay together; there is no replication in interkinesis.
trap: Trap (A): Accepting all, including plant-type cytokinesis for animal cells | Trap (B): Rejecting only one statement, missing that centromeres do not split in anaphase I | Trap (C): Also accepting statement IV, assuming every interphase-like stage has an S phase

question: The middle lamella that holds neighbouring plant cells together is made mainly of
explanation: The middle lamella is a layer mainly of calcium pectate which glues neighbouring cells together.
trap: Trap (A): Naming the main component of the primary wall | Trap (C): Naming another wall polysaccharide | Trap (D): Naming a secondary wall material

question: If the DNA content of a diploid cell in G1 is 2C, the DNA content of each cell at the end of meiosis I and at the end of meiosis II is respectively
explanation: After S phase the cell has 4C. Meiosis I gives two cells with 2C each (n chromosomes, two chromatids each); meiosis II gives cells with C.
trap: Trap (B): Assuming halving of chromosome number also halves DNA to C after meiosis I | Trap (C): Forgetting that the 4C content is shared between two cells in meiosis I | Trap (D): Assuming meiosis II, like interkinesis, leaves DNA content unchanged
concept: Cell cycle – DNA content through meiosis

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Leptotene (b) Zygotene (c) Pachytene (d) Diplotene (e) Diakinesis. Column II: (i) Terminalisation of chiasmata (ii) Compaction of chromosomes begins and they become visible (iii) Crossing over between non-sister chromatids (iv) Synapsis of homologous chromosomes (v) Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex.
explanation: Leptotene – compaction; zygotene – synapsis; pachytene – crossing over; diplotene – synaptonemal complex dissolves, chiasmata seen; diakinesis – terminalisation.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping synapsis and crossing over | Trap (B): Swapping the events of diplotene and diakinesis | Trap (C): Placing synapsis before chromosomes become visible
concept: Cell cycle – Stages of prophase I

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Collagen (b) GLUT-4 (c) Trypsin (d) Antibody. Column II: (i) Enables glucose transport into cells (ii) Fights infectious agents (iii) Intercellular ground substance (iv) Enzyme.
explanation: Collagen – intercellular ground substance; GLUT-4 – glucose transport; trypsin – enzyme; antibody – fights infectious agents.
trap: Trap (A): Treating GLUT-4 as an enzyme and trypsin as a transporter | Trap (B): Swapping the structural and defensive proteins | Trap (D): Treating collagen as an enzyme and trypsin as ground substance

question: The most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere is
explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world; RuBisCO is the most abundant in the whole biosphere.
trap: Trap (A): Giving the most abundant protein of the animal world | Trap (C): Choosing a common structural protein of hair and nails | Trap (D): Choosing the most familiar plasma protein

question: Assertion (A): Co-factors that are tightly bound to the apoenzyme are called co-enzymes. Reason (R): The association of co-enzymes with the apoenzyme is only transient, usually occurring during the course of catalysis.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: Tightly bound organic co-factors are prosthetic groups. Co-enzymes such as NAD associate only transiently with the apoenzyme.
trap: Trap (A): Using co-enzyme as a general name for every organic co-factor | Trap (B): Accepting the assertion and only doubting the link | Trap (C): Accepting the assertion and believing co-enzymes are permanently attached

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Adult human haemoglobin consists of four subunits, two of alpha type and two of beta type. II. Cellulose contains complex helices and therefore holds iodine. III. Lecithin is a simple triglyceride. IV. Adenosine is a nucleotide.
explanation: Only I is correct. Starch, not cellulose, forms helices that hold iodine; lecithin is a phospholipid; adenosine is a nucleoside.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement IV, confusing nucleoside with nucleotide | Trap (C): Also accepting III and IV, missing the phosphate in lecithin | Trap (D): Accepting all, including the property of starch for cellulose

question: The splitting of water during the light reaction is associated with
explanation: Water splitting is associated with PS II on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane; it supplies electrons to PS II and releases protons and oxygen.
trap: Trap (A): Assuming the photosystem numbered first acts first | Trap (B): Placing a membrane-linked event in the site of the dark reaction | Trap (D): Confusing proton release into the lumen with the enzyme that uses the gradient

question: How many ATP molecules are used in the regeneration step of the Calvin cycle for every CO2 molecule fixed?
explanation: Reduction uses 2 ATP and 2 NADPH per CO2; regeneration of RuBP needs 1 ATP for phosphorylation. Total 3 ATP per CO2.
trap: Trap (A): Giving the total ATP needed per CO2 for the whole cycle | Trap (B): Giving the ATP used in the reduction step | Trap (D): Assuming regeneration is only a rearrangement of sugars needing no energy

question: Substrate level phosphorylation in the TCA cycle occurs during the conversion of
explanation: During conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinic acid a molecule of GTP is synthesised; this is substrate level phosphorylation.
trap: Trap (B): Confusing decarboxylation steps with ATP-forming steps | Trap (C): Confusing the FAD-reducing step with direct ATP synthesis | Trap (D): Confusing an NAD-reducing step with direct ATP synthesis

question: When proteins are the respiratory substrate, the respiratory quotient is about
explanation: RQ is 1 for carbohydrates, about 0.7 for fats and about 0.9 for proteins.
trap: Trap (A): Giving the value for carbohydrates | Trap (B): Giving the value for fats | Trap (C): Assuming complex substrates release more CO2 than the O2 consumed

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. RuBisCO has a much greater affinity for CO2 when the CO2 : O2 ratio is nearly equal. II. In photorespiration there is no synthesis of ATP or NADPH. III. C4 plants show a high rate of photorespiration. IV. The first stable product of CO2 fixation in C4 plants is 3-PGA.
explanation: I and II are correct. C4 plants lack photorespiration, and their first product is the 4-carbon oxaloacetic acid.
trap: Trap (A): Rejecting statement I, assuming RuBisCO prefers O2 | Trap (C): Also accepting statement IV, giving the C3 product for C4 plants | Trap (D): Accepting all, including photorespiration in C4 plants

question: A filament of the green alga Cladophora was placed in a suspension of aerobic bacteria and illuminated with light split by a prism. The bacteria accumulated mainly in the regions of blue and red light. What does this experiment establish?
option_A: Aerobic bacteria are attracted to blue and red light
option_B: Green light is the most effective for photosynthesis
option_C: The oxygen evolved comes from carbon dioxide
option_D: It gives the first action spectrum of photosynthesis, resembling the absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
explanation: Engelmann used the bacteria to detect sites of oxygen evolution; their accumulation in blue and red light gave the first action spectrum of photosynthesis.
trap: Trap (A): Reading the bacteria, which are only detectors of oxygen, as the light-sensitive organism | Trap (B): Assuming the colour of the plant shows the light it uses | Trap (C): Mixing up this experiment with the question of the source of oxygen

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Auxin (b) Gibberellin (c) Kinetin (d) Ethylene. Column II: (i) Ripened oranges hastening ripening of stored bananas (ii) Coleoptile tips of oat seedlings (iii) 'Bakanae' disease of rice seedlings (iv) Autoclaved herring sperm DNA.
explanation: Auxin – Went, Avena coleoptile; gibberellin – Kurosawa, bakanae disease; kinetin – Skoog and Miller, autoclaved herring sperm DNA; ethylene – Cousins, ripened oranges.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping the discoveries of auxin and gibberellin | Trap (C): Swapping gibberellin and kinetin | Trap (D): Swapping kinetin and ethylene

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Glycolysis is also called the EMP pathway. II. NADH formed in glycolysis is reoxidised to NAD+ during fermentation. III. Complex V of the mitochondrial ETS is ATP synthase. IV. Oxidation of one NADH gives 3 ATP while one FADH2 gives 2 ATP. V. Acetyl CoA enters the TCA cycle by condensing with alpha-ketoglutaric acid.
explanation: I to IV are correct. Acetyl CoA condenses with oxaloacetic acid and water to form citric acid.
trap: Trap (A): Rejecting II and III as well, unsure of the reoxidation of NADH and of complex V | Trap (B): Rejecting statement II, thinking NADH is not used in fermentation | Trap (D): Accepting statement V, forgetting that acetyl CoA condenses with oxaloacetic acid
review_note: Faculty flag: Statement IV uses NCERT's NADH = 3 ATP / FADH2 = 2 ATP, not the modern 2.5/1.5.

question: Arithmetic growth is expressed mathematically as
explanation: In arithmetic growth only one daughter cell continues to divide; a linear curve is obtained, Lt = L0 + rt.
trap: Trap (B): Giving the expression for geometric growth | Trap (C): Multiplying instead of adding the growth term | Trap (D): Mixing the two expressions

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. Pollen grains of rice and wheat lose viability within 30 minutes of their release. II. The vegetative cell is small and floats in the cytoplasm of the generative cell. III. Pollen of Parthenium is sold as a food supplement. IV. The hilum is the opening left by the integuments at the tip of the ovule.
explanation: Only I is correct. The generative cell is small and floats in the vegetative cell; Parthenium pollen causes allergy; the opening is the micropyle.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement IV, confusing hilum with micropyle | Trap (C): Also accepting II and IV, reversing the two cells of the pollen grain | Trap (D): Accepting all, although Parthenium pollen is known for causing allergy

question: Assertion (A): Cleistogamous flowers produce an assured seed-set even in the absence of pollinators. Reason (R): In cleistogamous flowers the anthers and stigma are exposed to pollinating agents.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: Cleistogamous flowers never open; anthers and stigma lie close together, so they are invariably autogamous and seed-set is assured.
trap: Trap (A): Mixing up chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers while reading the reason | Trap (B): Treating the reason as a true but separate fact | Trap (D): Believing closed flowers cannot set seed

question: The coconut water of a tender coconut and its surrounding white kernel represent respectively
explanation: Coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm made up of thousands of nuclei; the white kernel is cellular endosperm.
trap: Trap (A): Reversing the two types | Trap (C): Confusing nucellar remains with endosperm | Trap (D): Assuming the food reserve of a seed is always a cotyledon

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. The embryo develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac. II. The zygote gives rise to the proembryo and subsequently to the globular, heart-shaped and mature embryo. III. In a grass embryo the scutellum is situated towards one side of the embryonal axis. IV. The coleoptile encloses the radicle and root cap. V. The epicotyl is the portion of the embryonal axis above the level of cotyledons.
explanation: I, II, III and V are correct. The radicle and root cap are enclosed by the coleorhiza; the coleoptile encloses the shoot apex and leaf primordia.
trap: Trap (A): Accepting only the micropylar-end statement | Trap (B): Rejecting three statements through confusion of epicotyl and hypocotyl | Trap (C): Rejecting one more true statement, such as the position of the scutellum

question: Which condition prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy?
option_D: Synchronised pollen release and stigma receptivity
explanation: In dioecious plants such as papaya, male and female flowers are on different plants, preventing both autogamy and geitonogamy.
trap: Trap (A): Forgetting that monoecy still allows geitonogamy | Trap (C): Choosing a device that ensures selfing | Trap (D): Choosing a condition that favours autogamy

question: In an artificial hybridisation programme using a female parent that bears unisexual flowers, which step is not needed?
option_B: Bagging of female flower buds before they open
option_C: Dusting the desired pollen on the receptive stigma
explanation: Emasculation removes anthers from bisexual flowers; with unisexual female flowers it is unnecessary, but bagging, dusting and rebagging are still required.
trap: Trap (B): Assuming unisexual flowers need no protection from unwanted pollen | Trap (C): Assuming pollination happens on its own once bagged | Trap (D): Assuming contamination is impossible after pollination

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Down's syndrome (b) Klinefelter's syndrome (c) Turner's syndrome (d) Phenylketonuria (e) Haemophilia. Column II: (i) 45 chromosomes with X0 (ii) Sex-linked recessive disorder of clotting (iii) Trisomy of chromosome 21 (iv) 47 chromosomes with XXY (v) Phenylalanine not converted into tyrosine.
explanation: Down's – trisomy 21; Klinefelter's – 47, XXY; Turner's – 45, X0; phenylketonuria – autosomal recessive metabolic error; haemophilia – sex-linked recessive.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping the karyotypes of Klinefelter's and Turner's syndromes | Trap (B): Assigning 47 chromosomes with XXY to Down's syndrome | Trap (C): Swapping the two Mendelian disorders

question: Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option. Column I: (a) Grasshopper (b) Drosophila (c) Birds (d) Honey bee. Column II: (i) Female heterogametic, ZW (ii) Males haploid, developing from unfertilised eggs (iii) Male has only one X chromosome besides autosomes (iv) Male heterogametic, XY.
explanation: Grasshopper – XO; Drosophila – XY; birds – ZW females; honey bee – haplodiploidy with haploid males.
trap: Trap (A): Swapping XO and XY types | Trap (B): Swapping birds and honey bee | Trap (D): Giving female heterogamety to Drosophila

question: Which of the following is a recessive trait in the pea plants studied by Mendel?
explanation: For pod colour, green is dominant and yellow recessive, although for seed colour yellow is dominant.
trap: Trap (A): Assuming the coloured form is recessive | Trap (C): Assuming the commoner-sounding position is recessive | Trap (D): Assuming the full pod is recessive

question: Human skin colour is assumed to be controlled by three genes A, B and C. In a cross AaBbCc × AaBbCc, the fraction of offspring expected to have the same genotype as the parents is
explanation: Probability of heterozygosity at each locus is 1/2; for three loci it is 1/2 × 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/8.
trap: Trap (A): Giving the fraction of the all-dominant or all-recessive genotype | Trap (B): Multiplying for only part of the genes with wrong factors | Trap (C): Using the probability for two heterozygous loci only

question: How many of the following statements are correct? I. The law of independent assortment holds for genes located very close together on the same chromosome. II. In Antirrhinum, the F2 phenotypic and genotypic ratios for flower colour are both 1 : 2 : 1. III. Henking discovered the Y chromosome. IV. Thalassemia is a qualitative defect of the globin molecule.
explanation: Only II is correct. Tightly linked genes do not assort independently; Henking traced the X body; thalassemia is a quantitative problem of too few globin molecules.
trap: Trap (B): Also accepting statement IV, confusing thalassemia with sickle-cell anaemia | Trap (C): Also accepting III and IV, mistaking Henking's X body for the Y chromosome | Trap (D): Accepting all, ignoring linkage

question: The chromosomal theory of inheritance was proposed by
option_D: de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak
explanation: Sutton and Boveri noted the parallel behaviour of chromosomes and genes; Sutton united chromosomal segregation with Mendelian principles.
trap: Trap (A): Naming the scientist who verified it experimentally in Drosophila | Trap (B): Naming the proposer of the laws of inheritance | Trap (D): Naming the rediscoverers of Mendel's work

question: A typical nucleosome contains about how many base pairs of DNA helix?
explanation: The negatively charged DNA is wrapped around the positively charged histone octamer to form a nucleosome containing 200 bp of DNA helix.
trap: Trap (A): Giving the number of base pairs in one turn of the helix | Trap (B): Recalling a figure from outside NCERT for the core particle | Trap (D): Overestimating from the idea of a chromatin loop
review_note: Faculty flag: Keyed to NCERT's 'about 200 bp' per nucleosome (146 bp core is a listed trap).

question: Assertion (A): Replication is discontinuous on one of the two template strands at a replication fork. Reason (R): DNA-dependent DNA polymerases catalyse polymerisation only in the 5' to 3' direction.
option_A: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_B: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_C: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_D: Assertion is false but Reason is true
